metadata.title: Coleman & Steele Course Reference Map

source_reference.full_title: Experimentation, Validation, and Uncertainty Analysis for Engineers
source_reference.authors: Hugh W. Coleman and W. Glenn Steele

sources: high_level_design/supporting_docs/Experimentation  Validation  and Uncertainty Analysis for Engineers - 2018 - Coleman.pdf

nodes.label: W1
nodes.title: Modeling Spine, Measurement Literacy & Experiment Design
nodes.description: Students locate measurement within the AMVF, distinguish measured from inferred quantities, and frame experimental work as an answer to a defined engineering question.

nodes.label: W2
nodes.title: Uncertainty Foundations: Power, Monte Carlo & First Deliverable
nodes.description: Students distinguish variability, error, and uncertainty; compute uncertainty in derived power estimates; compare partial-derivative and Monte Carlo approaches; and report results with interval meaning.

nodes.label: Lab 1
nodes.title: Power, Voltage, and the Language of Uncertainty
nodes.description: Students measure a simple resistor circuit, compute power using multiple models, propagate uncertainty, run Monte Carlo, and explain a complete engineering result.

nodes.label: W3
nodes.title: Quantitative Comparison, Validation Basics & Multiple Sensors
nodes.description: Students move from visual comparison to numerical agreement claims, distinguish calibration from validation, and diagnose sensor/model disagreements.

nodes.label: W4
nodes.title: Integration: Full Phase I Pipeline & Tier 1 Phase 1 Report
nodes.description: Students read model equations as experimental design documents, rank dominant uncertainty sources, perform calibration work, and assemble the full Tier 1 Phase 1 report.

nodes.label: W5
nodes.title: Cross-Prediction, Lightning Talks & Peer Assessment
nodes.description: Students move from analyzing their own experiment to predicting another experiment before seeing data, then communicate and critique prediction-to-measurement arguments.

nodes.label: Tier 1
nodes.title: Forward Analysis, Blind Prediction & Synthesis
nodes.description: Students execute a provided experiment, estimate uncertainty, compare models and measurements, and then make a blind prediction for another group's experiment.

nodes.label: W6
nodes.title: Prediction Before Exposure & Formal Hypothesis Framing
nodes.description: Students formalize prediction-before-measurement, intended use, response features, acceptance criteria, and anomalous-pattern risk assessment for complex systems.

nodes.label: W7
nodes.title: Signal Conditioning, Sampling & DAQ Fundamentals
nodes.description: Students connect sensor behavior, filtering, sampling, quantization, and DAQ configuration to the credibility of experimental data.

nodes.label: W8
nodes.title: Model Adequacy, Discrepancy & Calibration Revisited
nodes.description: Students interpret residuals, classify discrepancy, review calibration status, and use measured outcomes to propose model or measurement improvements.

nodes.label: Tier 2
nodes.title: Predict, Execute, Analyze, Improve
nodes.description: Groups commit to predictions before exposure, compare outcomes using uncertainty-aware metrics, diagnose discrepancy, and propose targeted improvements.

nodes.label: W9
nodes.title: Statistical Comparison, Regression & Monte Carlo
nodes.description: Students compare datasets, distinguish statistical from engineering significance, use regression diagnostically, and propagate uncertainty through multi-variable systems.

nodes.label: W10
nodes.title: Tier 2 Report, Quad Chart Presentation & Peer Review
nodes.description: Students consolidate prediction, uncertainty, calibration, validation, and improvement evidence into a report and compact technical presentation.

nodes.label: W11
nodes.title: Experimental Design Principles, Hypothesis & Prior Art
nodes.description: Students launch the final design challenge by defining the model claim, hypothesis, variables, standards context, prior art, and the question the proposed experiment should answer.

nodes.label: W12
nodes.title: Instrumentation Strategy, Signal Conditioning & Beyond-Provided Hardware
nodes.description: Students select sensors and DAQ configuration, justify signal conditioning choices, and estimate expected measurement performance before committing to a design.

nodes.label: W13
nodes.title: V&V Planning, Intended Use & Oral Defense Preparation
nodes.description: Students assemble a full V&V plan with conceptual model, response features, validation metrics, accuracy requirements, prospective uncertainty, and intended-use logic.

nodes.label: Final
nodes.title: Experimental Design and V&V Plan
nodes.description: Students design an original experiment on paper, including model claim, instrumentation plan, prospective uncertainty analysis, validation metrics, and oral defense.

nodes.label: W14
nodes.title: Oral Defense, Communication & Peer Assessment
nodes.description: Students defend their V&V plans, evaluate peer and sample work, and critique whether experimental-design claims are technically supported.

nodes.label: W15
nodes.title: Integration, Reflection & Course Closure
nodes.description: Students connect the whole course arc back to the AMVF and the central question: how do you know this prediction is right? Coleman & Steele is used here as a review anchor rather than a new reading.

nodes.label: Purpose
nodes.title: Experiment Purpose and Intended Use
nodes.description: The experiment exists to answer a specific engineering question at a useful level of certainty, not merely to collect data.

nodes.label: Errors
nodes.title: Error Sources and Uncertainty Language
nodes.description: Students need a stable vocabulary for random effects, systematic effects, standard uncertainty, expanded uncertainty, and coverage basis.

nodes.label: Intervals
nodes.title: Coverage and Confidence Intervals
nodes.description: Intervals must be labeled by what they mean, how they were computed, and what coverage or confidence claim they support.

nodes.label: Propagation
nodes.title: Uncertainty Propagation
nodes.description: Derived engineering results inherit uncertainty through the measurement model; sensitivity matters as much as input quality.

nodes.label: Planning
nodes.title: Uncertainty as a Design Tool
nodes.description: Prospective uncertainty analysis can decide whether an experiment is worth running before hardware or lab time is spent.

nodes.label: Systematics
nodes.title: Systematic Uncertainty, Calibration and Correlation
nodes.description: Calibration, correlated inputs, test sequence, and measurement-chain assumptions often dominate whether a validation claim is credible.

nodes.label: Regression
nodes.title: Regression and Model Fit Uncertainty
nodes.description: Regression is useful for describing trends and uncertainty in fitted relationships, but fit quality alone is not model validation.

nodes.label: Validation
nodes.title: Validation of Simulations
nodes.description: Validation asks whether model predictions are adequate for the intended use, with uncertainty in both experiment and simulation considered.

nodes.label: Dynamics
nodes.title: Dynamic Instrument Response
nodes.description: Instrument dynamics affect whether the measurement chain can capture the behavior the model claims to predict.

nodes.label: C&S 1-1 to 1-2
nodes.title: Experimentation and Experimental Approach
nodes.description: Use these opening sections for why experiments are necessary, how uncertainty sets the useful resolution of a comparison, and what questions an experimental program must answer.
nodes.student_use: Good for Week 1 framing, AMVF motivation, hypothesis formation, and intended-use language.

nodes.label: C&S 1-3
nodes.title: Basic Concepts and Definitions
nodes.description: Use this section cluster for errors, uncertainties, random and systematic effects, standard uncertainties, combined uncertainty, repetition, replication, and coverage language.
nodes.student_use: The best first stop for Lab 1 uncertainty vocabulary and oral interview preparation.

nodes.label: C&S 1-4
nodes.title: Results from Data Reduction Equations
nodes.description: Use this when the reported result is computed from multiple measured variables rather than directly measured.
nodes.student_use: Helpful for power equations in Lab 1 and any derived quantity in Tier 1, Tier 2, or E3.

nodes.label: C&S 1-5
nodes.title: Guides and Standards
nodes.description: Use this to connect course uncertainty and validation practice to professional guides and standards.
nodes.student_use: Useful in Week 1 standards framing and E3 source justification.

nodes.label: C&S 2-1
nodes.title: Monte Carlo Coverage Intervals for a Single Measured Variable
nodes.description: Use this for the single-variable Monte Carlo interval idea before students generalize Monte Carlo to derived quantities.
nodes.student_use: Useful when explaining what a Monte Carlo coverage interval means in Lab 1.

nodes.label: C&S 2-2
nodes.title: Confidence Intervals for a Single Measured Variable: Random Errors
nodes.description: Use this for distributions, Gaussian assumptions, confidence intervals, samples, prediction intervals, and outlier treatment when only random errors are considered.
nodes.student_use: Good support for interpreting repeated measurements and scatter.

nodes.label: C&S 2-3
nodes.title: Single Measured Variable: Random and Systematic Errors
nodes.description: Use this for systematic standard uncertainty and expanded uncertainty for a single measured variable.
nodes.student_use: Directly relevant when Lab 1 uses datasheet-based Type B inputs for voltage, current, or resistance.

nodes.label: C&S 2-4
nodes.title: Uncertainty of Uncertainty Estimates
nodes.description: Use this as a deeper reference for uncertainty in the interval limits themselves and design implications of high-confidence intervals.
nodes.student_use: Optional extension for students asking how certain the uncertainty estimate is.

nodes.label: C&S 3-1
nodes.title: General vs. Detailed Uncertainty Analysis
nodes.description: Use this to distinguish rough planning-level uncertainty analysis from a more complete detailed analysis.
nodes.student_use: Helpful when deciding how much uncertainty work is expected for a given assignment stage.

nodes.label: C&S 3-2
nodes.title: Monte Carlo Propagation of Uncertainties
nodes.description: Use this for propagating uncertain inputs through a data reduction equation using Monte Carlo simulation.
nodes.student_use: Directly relevant for Lab 1 Monte Carlo and later multi-input simulations.

nodes.label: C&S 3-3
nodes.title: Taylor Series Propagation of Uncertainties
nodes.description: Use this for partial-derivative uncertainty propagation and input sensitivity in derived results.
nodes.student_use: Directly relevant for Lab 1 power equations, Tier 1 derived quantities, and E3 prospective uncertainty.

nodes.label: C&S 3-4
nodes.title: MCM Coverage Intervals and TSM Expanded Uncertainty
nodes.description: Use this when comparing Monte Carlo coverage intervals to Taylor series expanded uncertainty.
nodes.student_use: Good for Lab 1 sections that compare partial-derivative and Monte Carlo results numerically.

nodes.label: C&S 3-5 to 3-6
nodes.title: General Uncertainty Examples and Spreadsheet Implementation
nodes.description: Use this as an implementation-oriented example of uncertainty propagation for engineering calculations.
nodes.student_use: Helpful for students who need a worked structure for MATLAB or spreadsheet-style uncertainty analysis.

nodes.label: C&S 4-1 to 4-3
nodes.title: TSM for Experiment Planning
nodes.description: Use these sections for using Taylor series uncertainty analysis before the experiment to plan measurements and judge feasibility.
nodes.student_use: Strong fit for Tier 1 predict-from-specs and E3 instrumentation planning.

nodes.label: C&S 4-4 to 4-6
nodes.title: Planning Examples and Presentation of Results
nodes.description: Use these examples to see how uncertainty analysis can indicate design changes and how results can be presented from actual applications.
nodes.student_use: Good optional support for E3 design tradeoffs and polished uncertainty reporting.

nodes.label: C&S 5-1 to 5-2
nodes.title: Detailed Uncertainty Analysis Overview
nodes.description: Use this for the overall methodology of detailed uncertainty analysis once students move beyond introductory examples.
nodes.student_use: Useful for Tier 2 and final project students who need a more complete workflow.

nodes.label: C&S 5-3
nodes.title: Determining Random Uncertainty of an Experimental Result
nodes.description: Use this for repeated-trial random uncertainty in an experimental result.
nodes.student_use: Helpful when distinguishing random scatter from systematic discrepancy in Week 3, Tier 1, or Tier 2.

nodes.label: C&S 6-1
nodes.title: Estimating Systematic Uncertainties
nodes.description: Use this for systematic uncertainty estimates, property-value uncertainty, calibration-related uncertainty, and instrument effects.
nodes.student_use: Direct support for datasheet/calibration reasoning in Lab 1, Tier 2, and E3.

nodes.label: C&S 6-2
nodes.title: Correlated Systematic Error Effects
nodes.description: Use this when multiple inputs share an error source or calibration basis and independence assumptions may fail.
nodes.student_use: Recommended for advanced Tier 2/E3 uncertainty budgets with correlated inputs.

nodes.label: C&S 6-3
nodes.title: Comparative Testing
nodes.description: Use this for difference or ratio comparisons between test results.
nodes.student_use: Useful for multi-sensor comparisons, Tier 1 synthesis, and Tier 2 improvement claims.

nodes.label: C&S 6-4
nodes.title: Additional Considerations in Experiment Execution
nodes.description: Use this for test point choice, test sequence, DOE relationship, jitter programs, transient testing, and digital DAQ error comments.
nodes.student_use: Useful for Week 7 DAQ awareness, Tier 2 execution critique, and E3 test planning.

nodes.label: C&S 7
nodes.title: Comprehensive Detailed Uncertainty Examples
nodes.description: Use this as a complete example bank for replication levels, balance checks, debugging, heat-exchanger tests, and comparative tests.
nodes.student_use: Optional but valuable when students want to see full engineering examples rather than isolated formulas.

nodes.label: C&S 8-1 to 8-2
nodes.title: Regression Overview and Reporting Regression Uncertainty
nodes.description: Use this for what regression uncertainty means and how regression uncertainty should be reported.
nodes.student_use: Best first stop for Week 9 regression interpretation.

nodes.label: C&S 8-3 to 8-6
nodes.title: Least Squares, Regression Examples, and Flow-Test Application
nodes.description: Use this for least-squares regression, uncertainty in coefficients and predicted values, multivariate regression, and an applied flow-test example.
nodes.student_use: Useful for Tier 2 reports with trend fitting or response-curve comparisons.

nodes.label: C&S 9-1 to 9-4
nodes.title: Validation Methodology, Nomenclature, and Approach
nodes.description: Use this for validation vocabulary, validation-variable framing, and the overall structure of a validation comparison.
nodes.student_use: Good conceptual anchor for Week 3, Tier 2 prediction gates, and the final V&V plan.

nodes.label: C&S 9-5 to 9-6
nodes.title: Verification and Interpretation of Validation Results
nodes.description: Use this for the verification-versus-validation distinction and interpretation of validation comparison results.
nodes.student_use: Helpful when students need to explain whether disagreement matters.

nodes.label: C&S 9-7
nodes.title: Estimating Validation Uncertainty
nodes.description: Use this for estimating validation uncertainty when the experimental validation value is directly measured or determined through a data reduction equation.
nodes.student_use: Direct support for Tier 2 validation reports and final V&V plan uncertainty adequacy.

nodes.label: C&S 9-8
nodes.title: Some Practical Points
nodes.description: Use this for practical judgment around validation studies and their interpretation.
nodes.student_use: Good short closing reference for final V&V plan critique.

nodes.label: C&S App. B
nodes.title: Taylor Series Method Derivation
nodes.description: Use this as the mathematical backup for the Taylor series propagation equation and coverage-factor assumptions.
nodes.student_use: Optional derivation support for Lab 1, Tier 2, or E3.

nodes.label: C&S App. C-D
nodes.title: Monte Carlo Model Comparison and Coverage Intervals
nodes.description: Use this as a deeper reference for Monte Carlo uncertainty models and shortest coverage interval logic.
nodes.student_use: Optional extension for Monte Carlo-heavy analyses.

nodes.label: C&S App. F
nodes.title: Dynamic Response of Instrument Systems
nodes.description: Use this to connect instrument dynamic response to sampling, filtering, and whether the sensor can represent the physical signal.
nodes.student_use: Helpful during DAQ/signal conditioning weeks and E3 sensor selection.

edges.description: Sections 1-1 and 1-2 frame why experiments are needed, what question the experiment answers, and how the required accuracy follows from intended use.
Section 1-3 is the main introductory vocabulary source for errors, uncertainties, systematic and random effects, repetition, replication, and coverage.
Section 1-4 introduces the idea that experimental results are often computed from multiple measured variables through a data reduction equation.
Section 1-5 helps connect course practices to guides and standards used in experimental uncertainty analysis and validation.
Section 2-1 gives the single-variable Monte Carlo coverage interval idea students later use in computational uncertainty work.
Section 2-2 supports confidence interval language, distributions, sample reasoning, prediction intervals, and outlier treatment for random effects.
Section 2-3 connects systematic standard uncertainty and expanded uncertainty to a single measured variable.
Section 2-3 gives students a more precise way to handle systematic uncertainty inputs from specifications and calibration information.
Section 2-4 is an advanced note on uncertainty in uncertainty estimates and the consequences for high-confidence design decisions.
Section 3-1 helps students decide whether an assignment needs a general or detailed uncertainty analysis.
Section 3-2 is the primary reference for Monte Carlo propagation through a data reduction equation.
Section 3-3 is the primary reference for Taylor series/partial-derivative uncertainty propagation.
Section 3-4 supports comparing Monte Carlo coverage intervals with Taylor series expanded uncertainty.
Sections 3-5 and 3-6 provide implementation-style examples students can adapt to MATLAB or spreadsheet workflows.
Sections 4-1 through 4-3 are the main source for applying uncertainty analysis during experiment planning.
Sections 4-4 through 4-6 show how planning uncertainty analysis can motivate experimental design changes and result presentation choices.
Sections 5-1 and 5-2 provide the broader workflow for detailed uncertainty analysis.
Section 5-3 supports random uncertainty estimates in experimental results from repeated observations.
Section 6-1 is the main source for estimating systematic uncertainties, including property and calibration-related examples.
Section 6-1 gives students more concrete examples of systematic uncertainty sources beyond the introductory vocabulary.
Section 6-2 supports correlated systematic uncertainty reasoning when error sources are not independent.
Section 6-3 supports comparative testing with differences and ratios, which maps well to multi-sensor and multi-condition comparisons.
Section 6-4 connects uncertainty reasoning to test sequence, test point choice, transient testing, and DAQ-related execution concerns.
Section 6-4 includes practical execution considerations that bridge into DAQ and transient measurement decisions.
Chapter 7 provides comprehensive examples of detailed uncertainty analysis, debugging, balance checks, and comparative tests.
Sections 8-1 and 8-2 are the most direct source for regression uncertainty and responsible reporting of fitted relationships.
Sections 8-3 through 8-6 provide least-squares methods, coefficient uncertainty, prediction uncertainty, multivariate regression, and an applied flow-test example.
Sections 9-1 through 9-4 are the primary entry point for validation methodology, nomenclature, and approach.
Sections 9-5 and 9-6 support verification-versus-validation distinctions and interpretation of validation results.
Section 9-7 is the key source for estimating validation uncertainty in direct and data-reduction-equation cases.
Section 9-8 provides practical points for interpreting validation work.
Appendix B is the backup for students who want the derivation and assumptions behind Taylor series uncertainty propagation.
Appendices C and D are optional extensions for Monte Carlo uncertainty modeling and interval construction.
Appendix F connects instrument dynamics to whether a measured signal is faithful to the physical behavior.
